transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I haven’t been able to let go of something that’s been going on for almost two years. After a commission I worked on, I became certain that a few people in the ensemble started trying to undermine my work quietly—through schedule changes, where people were seated, little comments during rehearsals, things like that. 

They’ve shown me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but it still feels clear to me that there’s something else behind it.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed since this situation started?
I wouldn’t say depressed, exactly. I’ve been upset and frustrated about it, and it weighs on me sometimes, but I haven’t really thought of it as sadness so much as feeling bothered by what happened.
Do you still believe that those people are trying to undermine your work?

Yes. I mean, I try to talk myself out of it sometimes, but I still believe it. It’s been almost two years, and I still can’t shake the feeling that after that commission, certain people in the ensemble were using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsals to undercut what I was doing. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, it still feels like there’s something else going on.
Have you been feeling hopeless about your situation?
I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. I do get worn down by it, like it feels stuck and hard to resolve. But I don’t think of it as having no way forward.
Do you think that your belief about people undermining your work is possibly not true?

I guess I can say it’s possible, in an abstract way. But honestly, it doesn’t feel not true to me. I’m here because for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the certainty that after that commission, a few people in the ensemble were quietly undermining my work—through schedule changes, seating choices, and those small comments in rehearsals. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, I still feel like there’s more behind it.
Do you think your belief about being undermined is based on facts or is it more of a gut feeling that you can't explain?

It feels based on facts to me, not just a gut feeling. I mean, the schedule changes, where people were seated, the little comments in rehearsal — those things actually happened. Other people show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but I still can’t shake the certainty that there was something underneath it, that a few people were trying to quietly undermine my work after the commission.
Do you think there's any chance that your interpretation of these events is incorrect?

I mean, I can admit there’s some chance, technically. But it doesn’t feel that way to me. For almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the certainty that after that commission, a few people in the ensemble were using the schedule changes, seating choices, and little rehearsal comments to undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, it still feels like there was something behind it.
Do you think other people share your belief that you were being undermined?

Not really. I’ve tried to explain it to a couple people, and they usually point to the emails or the rehearsal notes and say it was all normal. But to me, those explanations don’t really settle it. I still feel certain that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble were using the schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments to quietly undermine my work.
Do you think your belief about being undermined would change if everyone involved, including those you suspect, told you directly that they were not trying to undermine you?

Honestly, I don’t think it would change much. I’d hear them say it, and I might try to take it in, but I’d still feel like there was something underneath it. That’s been the problem for almost two years — even when there are emails or notes that supposedly explain the schedule changes or seating choices, I still can’t shake the certainty that a few of them were quietly undermining my work.
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy since this situation started?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve totally lost interest in music or the things I usually like, but this situation does make it harder to enjoy them sometimes. It’s more like it’s in the back of my mind, not that I stopped caring about everything.
Do you think your belief about being undermined is something that might be happening only in your mind?

I’ve thought about that, but no… it doesn’t feel like it’s just in my mind. I know people keep showing me emails or rehearsal notes that are supposed to explain the schedule changes or seating choices, but I still can’t shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people were quietly using those things, and little comments in rehearsals, to undermine my work.
Do you think there's any situation or evidence that could make you completely change your mind about being undermined?

I honestly don’t know what would make me completely change my mind. I guess if there were some clear explanation for every schedule change, seating choice, and the comments in rehearsal… but even when people show me emails or notes, it still doesn’t really settle it for me. I keep feeling certain that after the commission, a few people were using those things to quietly undermine my work.
Has your belief that you were being undermined affected your relationships with friends or family?

Not really with friends or family, no. I mean, I’ve been stressed about the ensemble situation, but outside of that I’m still getting my work done, keeping up with composing, and running most mornings. Things at home with my wife are basically steady.
Do you think your belief about being undermined is something that you are absolutely certain about, no matter what evidence is presented to you?

Yes… I’d say I’m very certain. That’s kind of why I’m here. For almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the feeling—really the certainty—that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and small comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, it doesn’t really change what I’m convinced is happening.
Do you think your belief about being undermined is something that you might be mistaken about?

I mean… in theory, anyone can be mistaken. But honestly, I don’t feel like I am about this. I’ve been unable to shake it for almost two years—that after the commission, certain people in the ensemble were using the schedule changes, seating choices, and little rehearsal comments to undermine me. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, it still doesn’t really change my mind.
Have you been experiencing any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since this situation started?
Not really, no. I mean, I’ve had some restless nights when I’m thinking about it, but I wouldn’t say my sleep or appetite has changed in a major way. Nothing that really stands out.
Do you think your belief about being undermined could be considered a delusion by others?

I can see that other people might call it that, yes. But from my side it doesn’t feel like some random belief. I’m here because for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and small rehearsal comments to quietly undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, it doesn’t really change what I think is happening.
